title: Exponential core and container force with gradient limit
purpose: Exercises the gradient limit (second value of `expecf` > 0) of the default exponential repulsive core and of the exponential container force in the `epsr` engine of EPSR [@soper1996,@soper2005]: beyond the limit the exponential is continued linearly so that the energy of strongly overlapping or escaped atoms cannot explode [@epsrmanual].
system: The EPSR-test system: a liquid mixture of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO, (CH3)2SO) and 400 water molecules (DMSO mole fraction 1/3; 3200 atoms) at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å (atomic number density 0.0881 atoms/Å³). DMSO uses EPSR's Lennard-Jones + Coulomb reference potential with methyl rotational groups; water uses SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charge parameters [@berendsen1987] with EPSR's flexible intramolecular geometry (O-H 0.976 Å). The empirical potential is refined against three neutron diffraction data sets of deuterated DMSO in D2O, in null-scattering H2O/D2O and in H2O (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), the isotope-substitution approach of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. As in EPSR-test-ex15 every DMSO carries an extra massless, uncharged Q site at its sulphur (3400 atoms) and water oxygens further than 4 Å from the nearest Q site are pulled back by an exponential container force. With `expecf 0.300 1.500` the core pcoefex·exp(ddiff) becomes pcoefex·gradlimit·(1 + ddiff - log(gradlimit)) for ddiff >= log(gradlimit), and the container force is limited in the same way.
inputs: `scripts/make_ex15.py ../../../EPSR-test . 4.0 0.5` (as EPSR-test-ex15: Q sites, 28 pairs, Q-O1 `rmaxex 4.0`, `pcoefexmax 0.5`, `iinit 1`), then `scripts/make_case.py`: `expecf 0.300 1.500` and the repulsive-core lines of EPSR-test-ex1 (`rminex pcoefex coordex`: S-S `4.0 0 0.1`, O1-O1 `2.6 0.5 0`, O1-H1 `1.5 0.2 0.05`).
verification: The README reports a gcov check of the Fortran: `generate_rp` executes both the linear and the `exp(ddiff)` term of the core with `gradlimit = 1.5`, and `en_containerforce` its exponential branch with 345 linear and 2055 exponential evaluations. EPSR-test-ex15 covers only the default `gradlimit = 1, loggradlimit = 0` of the container force and no exponential core, so this case adds both limited branches.
